lines.text: Every online store has a checkout. When it breaks, it costs a sale every single time, and often nobody notices, because nobody clicks through the whole journey. This is CheckoutGuard.
CheckoutGuard tests your checkout with Kane CLI, hands any bug it finds to a coding agent, and only calls a fix verified when Kane passes the journey again. And a person approves every merge.

Here's our demo store, Northwind Goods. I add a ceramic mug to the cart, and set the quantity to three. Three mugs at eighteen dollars should cost fifty-four. The cart says eighteen. That's the kind of bug that slips through.
This is the CheckoutGuard dashboard. At the top is the loop, with live numbers. Below are the three checkout journeys we test: the cart total, an expired coupon, and the order confirmation page.

Let's test the cart journey. CheckoutGuard runs Kane CLI with a plain-English objective: add the mug, set the quantity to three, and check that the subtotal is fifty-four dollars. Kane drives a real browser, step by step, like a customer would.
Kane fails the journey, and says why: after the quantity changed to three, the subtotal still showed eighteen dollars.
The evidence page keeps everything Kane saw: the journey, every check it made, its diagnosis, and a screenshot from the moment it failed.
Now I ask for a fix. Kane's evidence becomes the brief for Claude Code. It works in an isolated copy of the store, with file tools only. It has no shell, no web access, and it can't edit the tests.
The agent finds the bug in the pricing code. It added each product's price once and ignored the quantity. The fix is one line. Then the unit checks run, with no regressions.
Now the part that matters. Kane runs the exact same journey against the patched store. Only when Kane passes it is the repair marked verified.
Nothing merges on its own. I review the diff, and Kane's before and after screenshots. Every repair also has a report I can download, so the decision can be checked later.
It looks right, so I approve, and the fix is merged.
CheckoutGuard caught and fixed all three seeded checkout bugs this way, and Kane CLI verified every fix. Every checkout tested. Every fix verified.
